questions.stem: Which of the following is a stated limitation of automatic indexing?

options.A: It cannot analyse titles, abstracts, full text or metadata.
options.B: It is too slow to handle large-scale indexing.
options.C: Algorithmic context may be misunderstood and semantic relationships may be missed, so human quality control is still generally necessary.
options.D: It requires an indexer to manually assign every term to a document.

questions.explanation: Automatic indexing is rapid and suits very large collections, but algorithmic context may be misunderstood, ambiguous terms misinterpreted and semantic relationships missed, so human quality control is still generally necessary.

questions.stem: Which group lists the three computer-assisted indexing software packages described in this chapter?

options.B: Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed/MEDLINE
options.C: Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning and text mining
options.D: ERIC, Chemical Abstracts and Library and Information Science Abstracts

questions.explanation: CINDEX, Sky Index and Macrex are the widely recognised computer-assisted indexing packages named in section 14.3; the other options are databases or AI techniques.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a hyperlinked index and a dynamic index?

options.A: A hyperlinked index links an entry directly to the relevant section of the document, while a dynamic index updates automatically whenever the underlying document is revised.
options.B: A dynamic index links an entry directly to the relevant page, while a hyperlinked index must be completely reworked after any change to pagination.
options.C: A hyperlinked index can only link to figures and tables, while a dynamic index can only link to external websites.
options.D: A dynamic index is used only for printed books, while a hyperlinked index is used only for online databases.

questions.explanation: In a hyperlinked index an entry links directly to the relevant section so the reader can click through immediately; dynamic indexes update automatically when the document changes, unlike a printed index that must be reworked after any change to pagination.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a task that AI can assist with in indexing and abstracting?

options.A: Deciding the appropriate level of specificity for an ambiguous term
options.B: Determining which concepts are truly significant to a specialised audience
options.C: Extracting keywords automatically from a document
options.D: Judging meanings that are implied rather than stated

questions.explanation: Section 14.5 lists extracting keywords automatically among the tasks AI can assist with; judging specificity, significance and implied meanings are examples of work that still requires the human indexer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a stated challenge of digital or AI-assisted indexing?

options.C: Improved accessibility through searchable, navigable indexes
options.D: Easier correction and revision of entries

questions.explanation: Section 14.7 lists inconsistencies in AI-generated terminology among the recurring challenges; faster preparation, improved accessibility and easier correction are benefits, not challenges.
